s: undeservingly; in an unearned way; by chance
Mein Chef ist zu seinem Job gekommen wie Pilatus ins Credo.
My boss got his job like Pilate got into the creed.

s: as one pleases (mostly implying that it does not make a difference)
Soll ich hier anfangen oder da? – Das kannst du machen wie Pastor Nolte.
Should I start here or there? – Suit yourself.
wie Pastor Nolte.et: Literally, “like reverend Nolte”. From the rhyme: der machte es, wie er’s wollte (“he did it as he liked”). Attested since at least the 1910s. More recently re-popularised by an episode of the series Stromberg (German adaptation of The Office).
